thread:
oncall-bot: Pager alert: GPU pool 'prod-eu-gpu' capacity-critical (queue depth 98%, pending jobs 3.2k). Autoscaler failing to scale beyond 60 nodes. Marking severity: P1.

elena: ack — I'm oncall. Pulling queue metrics now. Any obvious customer-facing errors? :mag:

samir: seeing a bunch of backend logs with recurring CUDA Xid 116 and OOM entries from kubelet on several nodes. Suspect driver/runtime instability shrinking effective capacity.

kevin: Confirmed. Paste from one node (sensitive fields redacted):
```
[2026-03-15T02:12:11Z] nvidia: Xid 116: GPU access fault at 0x7ff... kernel panic avoided, process killed
[2026-03-15T02:12:11Z] containerd: oom kill process 'python inference_worker' pid=4523
```
Multiple nodes show similar patterns over last 10m.

elena: thanks. Is autoscaler hitting the configured `max_nodes`? What are current min/max?

ops-bot: Autoscaler config for prod-eu-gpu: min=20, max=60, target_util=0.75. Current nodes=60 (all requested), pending scale_up requests failing with `driver_registration_timeout` on 14 nodes.

samir: driver_registration_timeout likely because the node's GPU driver keeps crashing on init (Xid waves). Even if we scale, nodes never register usable GPUs.

elena: immediate mitigation options: 1) pause non-critical batch jobs (low priority) -> frees queue; 2) increase autoscaler max temporarily; 3) remove/cordon nodes showing repeated Xid/OOM so scheduler won't send new pods there; 4) roll driver to previous known-good build on a handful of nodes. Thoughts?

kevin: agree. Start with pausing low-priority queues and cordoning suspicious nodes. Rolling drivers across all nodes is risky right now. We can hotpatch a driver variant on a small canary pool (3 nodes) to verify.

ryan: I'll take on cordon/drain for the worst offenders. Which nodes? list: eu-prod-gpu-23, -24, -31, -45.

lia: tagging customers impacted: 'fast-retry' and 'batch-embed' have growing error rates. Notified account reps; raising priority for fast-retry customers that are in prod.

elena: samir — can you open a small canary with driver v525.85 (previous stable) and run smoke workloads?

samir: spinning canary 3 nodes now with v525.85. Running a synthetic 1k token workload loop. Logs linked: https://internal.redwood/logs/5201234567/canary (internal).

kevin: added temporary autoscaler override: `max=90` and `scale_cooldown=30s` to try absorbing backlog while we cordon nodes. Make sure to watch driver registration failures — autoscaler might create nodes that never register.

ops-bot: Action taken: paused queue 'batch-low' via queue-controller (API call id abc123). Paused 2,100 jobs.

elena: good. Ryan, proceed with cordon/drain on the four nodes. Use graceful drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Notify here when each node completes.

ryan: cordon eu-prod-gpu-23 -> done. drain in progress. Pod eviction rate slow due to PVs, force eviction on non-prod pods.

ryan: eu-prod-gpu-23 drained and cordoned, removed from scheduler. eu-prod-gpu-24 cordoned, observed immediate Xid spiking on kernel logs, skipping drain to avoid mass evictions.

kevin: If Xid spiking on cordon means driver instability persists even when scheduling is stopped — these nodes need reboot + driver rollback. Samir, can you push a reboot + driver re-install for -24 and -31?

samir: pushing reboot+driver rollback now via infra playbook: `scripts/driver_rollback.sh --nodes eu-prod-gpu-24,eu-prod-gpu-31 --driver v525.85 --reboot`. Triggered at 02:26Z.

oncall-bot: Event note: manual mitigation actions recorded (pause queue, autoscaler max bump, cordon/drain, driver rollback).

lia: Customer impact update: error rate for fast-retry peaked at 12% but is now 5% after pause + autoscaler bump. Several enterprise customers reported increased latency; support sent templated update.

elena: can we confirm queue depth trend?

ops-bot: Queue depth timeline (recent): 02:08Z=3100, 02:18Z=2600, 02:30Z=1200, 02:38Z=420. Backlog dropping, token throughput increasing on stable canary nodes.

kevin: canary nodes registered successfully and handled synthetic load without Xid/OOM for 22 minutes. rolling further drivers onto 6 additional nodes in waves of 2.

samir: rollback completed on -24 and -31 and both came back healthy (nvidia-smi shows no Xid). eu-prod-gpu-45 still showing intermittent OOM, isolating.

elena: good. Moving to containment -> mitigated. Next actions: 1) immediate post-incident runbook draft, 2) revert autoscaler max to normal (max=60) after backlog cleared, 3) schedule full driver rollout to stable version with canary gating, 4) postmortem owner?

ryan: I'll own postmortem; assigning to SRE+Runtime team. Will include timeline, root cause hypothesis (driver regression causing Xid wave -> effective capacity drop -> autoscaler saturation), and recommended controls (circuit-breaker on driver rollout, better node health gating for autoscaler).

lia: communicating final customer update: latency normalized, no ongoing errors for impacted customers.

oncall-bot: Resolution note: backlog drained, node registrations stable. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.

elena: thanks team. We'll reconvene tomorrow for a short blameless postmortem. Adding follow-ups to runbook: detect Xid surge -> automatic temporary pause of low-priority queues, autoscaler guard to avoid creating nodes that fail to register, and health-check gating. :white_check_mark:

samir: adding logs & kernel traces to the incident folder: https://internal.redwood/incidents/5201234567/artifacts

kevin: ok to handoff to daytime oncall (ryan) in 30m.

ryan: taking handoff. leaving this channel open for any regressions.

elena: handoff accepted. Closing communication channel in 1h if stable. Thanks all. :pray:
